smallest_supported_claim: This separate ordinary, no-debug account began from the native-saved daytime open footing with a player-visible zombie rider.  The rider applied visible ranged pressure after the player chose to move; the account reached a real death terminal state before it could establish a safe counterplay or disengagement, bounded recovery, or intermittence.
causal_account: The account was freshly source/executable-bound to the zero-credit saved footing and used no debug action.  Safe mode was switched off, then the player chose a westward movement.  The next World observation records the rider's arrow, torso damage, bleeding, and stagger.  The player opened the native inventory and selected the active smartphone's advertised flashlight-off menu option, then chose another westward movement.  The resulting terminal observation records an actual avatar death.  This is evidence of player-legible pressure, not a causal attribution of the death solely to the rider, nor evidence of successful disengagement, recovery, or later intermittence.

material_deviations: The account died before a safe counterplay or disengagement, recovery, or intermittence observation could be made; therefore no native save-and-quit lifecycle was available for this deceased account.
remaining_unknowns: Whether a survivable ordinary footing can demonstrate rider-specific counterplay or disengagement.
Whether pressure can subside and later recur under ordinary play without conflating other hostiles or environmental factors.
